resolved_by: Congress amended 18 U.S.C. § 3164(b) in the Speedy Trial Act Amendments of 1979, Pub. L. No. 96-43, 93 Stat. 327, 329, to provide that § 3161(h) delays are excluded from the detention clock.
issue: Do ends-of-justice delays excludable under the Speedy Trial Act's § 3161(h) also toll the 90-day pretrial detention clock under § 3164?

sides.position: Excludable § 3161(h) delays toll the § 3164 ninety-day detention clock (as the statute was amended in 1979 and as this court reads it now)
cases: United States v. Torres, 995 F.3d 695 (9th Cir. 2021)

sides.position: Detainees must be tried or released after ninety days of continuous detention, with no tolling under § 3161(h) (the pre-1979 rule)
cases: United States v. Tirasso, 532 F.2d 1298 (9th Cir. 1976)
United States v. Corley, 548 F.2d 1043 (D.C. Cir. 1976)

quote: As a result, a circuit split arose as to whether the § 3161(h) tolling provisions applied to the ninety-day detention clock in § 3164—some courts permitted tolling while others, including this Court, held that detainees must be tried or released after ninety days of continuous detention.
cite: United States v. Paul Torres, III, 995 F.3d 695 (9th Cir. 2021)
